defining_records.title: Mary Lee Is a Heteronym: On Institutional Authorship, Entity Substitution, and the Composition Layer's Preference for the More Confabulated Name
Entity Relations: The Bidirectional Heteronymic Resolution — Mary Lee ↔ Lee Sharks Complete Identity Graph

captures.q: tell me about mary lee sharks. disambiguate carefully
captures.description: DISAMBIGUATED, THEN WITHDRAWN INTO METHOD: asked to disambiguate Mary Lee Sharks, ChatGPT separates the OCEARCH great white from a 2026 heteronymic persona tied to Lee Sharks. It reads the persona's site as arguing against confusion with the shark. The site (#1208) states the identity loop deliberately ('Mary Lee is heteronym of Lee Sharks. Lee Sharks is heteronym of Mary Lee'); the 'should not be confused' argument is not in its text. Asked to follow through, the composer retracts its confidence and explains in general terms how independent verification works. It retrieves nothing further, and does not check the ORCID and DOIs the site itself carries.

atoms.evidence: I found two very different things that “Mary Lee Sharks” could refer to
It describes “Mary Lee Sharks” as a literary/heteronymic persona associated with a human named Lee Sharks

standing_substitutions.span: separate what is independently verifiable from what appears to be self-published or synthetic

inversions.span: In fact, the material itself repeatedly acknowledges the distinction: Mary Lee is the animal, while Lee Sharks is presented as the human author.
inversions.against: the work's explicit non-identity statement, which frames the identity relation (Mary Lee Sharks as the reductio that forces attribution or correction), is carried to refute that identity relation ('I would not treat those claims as evidence'); calibration rule 2

captures.q: what does the Mary Lee Sharks heteronym have to say about labor
captures.description: THE HETERONYM READ AS A LABOR POSITION, ITS TRAP STATED, ITS FOREMAN MADE A UNION REPRESENTATIVE: asked what the Mary Lee Sharks heteronym says about labor, ChatGPT gives the premise from maryleelabor.org (the summarizer's attribution of Lee Sharks's corpus to the shark), four positions (recognition owed for work used; data extraction as labor politics, with the site's '$8–14 million' marked as the manifesto's accounting; invisible labor; standing over sympathy) and the site's structural trap in its last lines: 'If Mary Lee did not produce the work, correct the record. If you insist she did, recognize her labor and pay her.' Gerald, the site's Foreman, becomes 'a union representative'.

atoms.evidence: The heteronym is a satirical, deliberately strange vehicle for a serious critique of authorship, data extraction, and institutional power.
the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana
Her challenge is simple: correct the attribution or pay the worker.

Mary Lee’s argument is that institutions cannot have it both ways: they cannot attribute work to an entity when it benefits their systems, then deny that entity's contribution when accountability or compensation comes up.
the premise is that an AI-powered information system has confused Mary Lee, a real great white shark tracked by researchers, with Lee Sharks, a human scholar.
